//: Farm workspace root. The farm IS its own monorepo framework — Deno workspaces + a tiny affected orchestrator (tools/affected.mjs) — so there is NO Turborepo/Nx and NO node_modules. Packages below are workspace members; apps stay pure Deno (resolved at serve time by each index.html import map); CI verifies only the apps a change actually reaches.
//core: THE dependency. Execution rides the jsr: pin below (deno realm — the registry cache); the FILE tree for /_rt serving and the build rides the npm-compat tarball in package.json. Bump = the version here + in package.json, then deno task install.
//tasks: Tools run via explicit jsr: specifiers — the registry realm by construction. (A CLI arg is never import-mapped, and a bare @microspec/core/* arg byonm-resolves into node_modules — the npm realm, where jsr:/https imports are refused.) The version appears in imports, package.json and these tasks; deno task install after a bump.

tasks.red: gh run view $(gh run list --workflow=verify.yml --limit 1 --json databaseId --jq '.[0].databaseId') --log-failed | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | grep -E '✗'

//gates: THE pre-push block, now an 8n8 flow (tools/8n8/nodes.mjs) instead of a `&&` chain. Same checks, one superset node (the registry's own contract test), 45.5s -> 24.4s measured, because independent nodes have no reason to be sequential. The reason it stopped being `&&`: a chain stops at the FIRST red, so one round answers one boolean and the next four failures stay hidden — and `deno task gates | grep ...` returns grep's exit code, which is how a red farm got pushed. The runner runs every node whose dependencies are green, prints each failure IN FULL with its node id and argv, and exits non-zero on the count. Running all but one of these is how a stale service-worker manifest reached CI twice, so `sw` is a node, not a habit: an import graph changes the moment a view adopts a kit component. `kit` is the same shape one level up - tools/mcp/kit.json is GENERATED from packages/runtime/ui.js, so touching the kit without `deno task kit` leaves every agent reading a signature that no longer exists.
//8n8: The pipeline registry itself. `deno task 8n8 --list` prints every node, whether it is a deterministic script or still an agent hand-off, and the share of the pipeline that no longer needs a model. n8n has a human draw the graph and a machine run it; here the agent does the work and a run that proved itself FREEZES into a script node - packages/gen/authorless.mjs is the existence proof. The number only goes up.
//red: Print CI failures IN FULL. Never pipe this through `cut` or `head -c`: the gate names the offending element and its geometry, and truncating that turns a measurement back into a guess — three commits were spent moving the wrong element because its class name was cut at 170 characters.
